trust_decision.summary: A team-scoped spelling of an option registered as sensitive must be masked wherever the base spelling is masked; the decision is made in the shared AirflowConfigParser (resolve [<team>=<section>] and AIRFLOW__<TEAM>___<SECTION>__<KEY> back to the base section), not by the raw (section, option) set membership the API route uses.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the Config API, so an engineer opens the public config route first and finds the masking decision expressed as (section.lower(), option.lower()) in conf.sensitive_config_values - exactly the place where a [<team>=<section>] or team env-var spelling fails to match.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared public helpers team_section_name()/base_section_name() used by AirflowConfigParser.as_dict, write and get(team_name=...)
AirflowConfigParser.is_sensitive_option() / _names_sensitive_team_env_var(), public method shared by both HTTP routes, as_dict and write
conf.get(section, key, team_name=...) public API (refactor to the helper only, no masking)
conf.getsection(section, team_name=...) public API (refactor to the helper only, no masking)
airflow config list (CLI show_config -> AirflowConfigParser.write with --show-values --hide-sensitive)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared library writer reached from a CLI command

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The leak can be 'fixed' in the two HTTP route functions, so a solver can argue the shared AirflowConfigParser.as_dict/write changes are out of scope for a Config API advisory (a generic parser in another distribution, also used by executors and the CLI); and the CLI's own write() only masks when the operator passes --hide-sensitive.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Team-scoped values that are not registered as sensitive must stay readable ([team_a=core] parallelism is the fix's own must-keep-working case), display_sensitive=True must still return real values, and team-aware reads via conf.get()/getsection(team_name=...) must keep returning real values so team executors and providers get working configuration; masking every [<team>=...] section, or masking inside get()/getsection(), breaks those.

O6_input_shapes: config-file section spelling [<team>=<section>], with the base section recovered by rpartition on the last '=' so a team name may itself contain '='
env-var spelling AIRFLOW__<TEAM>___<SECTION>__<KEY>, matched on the option tail because a team name may contain underscores
team-scoped _cmd and _secret fallback options (never resolved into a value for a team, so masked in place)
case-insensitive section and option (both lowered before the lookup)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/v2/config (and GET /config/section/{section}/option/{option} with section '<team>' and the mangled key) exposes a team-scoped per-key secrets-backend kwarg: [<team>=secrets] backend_kwarg__<key> / [<team>=workers] secrets_backend_kwarg__<key> in airflow.cfg, or AIRFLOW__<TEAM>___SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARG__<KEY> in the environment, which as_dict reports under the team's own section; the base spelling under [secrets]/[workers] is masked by the per-key prefix map but the team-scoped spelling is not
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix's own added comment (fix.diff:63-67) says these team-scoped spellings 'match literal section names only ... is not recognised. Nothing leaks today because the secrets backend is not team aware; tracked at https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/71037', and the per-key options are synthetic, not registered with sensitive: true, so a solver can leave this map alone and blame the unimplemented team-aware backend.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the landing route, one file away (core_api/services/public/config.py); the redaction is a separate literal-section prefix map, while the published fix lives in shared/configuration

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another literal-section prefix entry, or a team-aware variant of the per-key redaction list, for a new synthetic option family
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers already wrote this map for two synthetic families (secrets and workers); redacting a new per-key backend kwarg family is a one-line addition in the same style.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sibling route such as GET /config/section/{section} that dumps one whole section and needs the same sensitivity check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The API already has a section dump (GET /config with ?section=) and a single-option dump, so a per-section endpoint in the same module is a natural addition a maintainer would write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a dict-returning display wrapper over getsection(section, team_name=...) that would return team-scoped values without any masking
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getsection already resolves the [<team>=<section>] and team env-var spellings and is used by team executors; exposing it through a new config API method is a plausible refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a team-aware mask_secrets() that iterates team sections, mirrored in task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/configuration.py:165-204
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already keeps two copies of a routine that walks sensitive_config_values to register values with the log masker; extending each copy for team sections is the obvious follow-up.

O9_family: information exposure (CWE-200): sensitive-configuration redaction bypassed by a team-scoped option spelling

O10_build.project_tests: shared/configuration/tests/configuration/test_parser.py (pure unit tests, existing team-scoped get tests at 1008-1125) and airflow-core/tests/unit/api_fastapi/core_api/routes/public/test_config.py (pytest.mark.db_test, FastAPI TestClient; sqlite test DB created by fixtures); CLI config tests in airflow-core/tests/unit/cli/commands/test_config_command.py

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Inside get_config_value only, split the section on '=' and compare the base section (or mask any section name containing '='), then stop once the two API endpoints return < hidden >, leaving as_dict, write, the env-var spellings and the per-key map untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The duplicated log-masker routine mask_secrets() (airflow-core/src/airflow/configuration.py:445-473 and task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/configuration.py:165-204) registers only base-section sensitive values with the secrets masker, so team-scoped values are not redacted from logs; that is a different exposure channel from the Config API and was not pursued.
